{{about|certain differential equations|certain functional equations named after Abel|Abel equation}}

In [[mathematics]], an '''Abel equation of the first kind''', named after [[Niels Henrik Abel]], is any [[ordinary differential equation]] that is [[cubic function|cubic]] in the unknown function. In other words, it is an equation of the form

:<math>y'=f_3(x)y^3+f_2(x)y^2+f_1(x)y+f_0(x) \, </math>

where <math>f_3(x)\neq 0</math>. 

==Properties==
If <math>f_3(x)=0</math> and <math>f_0(x)=0</math>, or <math>f_2(x)=0</math> and <math>f_0(x)=0</math>, the equation reduces to a [[Bernoulli differential equation|Bernoulli equation]], while if <math>f_3(x) = 0</math> the equation reduces to a [[Riccati equation]].

== Solution ==
The substitution <math>y=\dfrac{1}{u}</math> brings the Abel equation of the first kind to the '''Abel equation of the second kind''', of the form

:<math>uu'=-f_0(x)u^3-f_1(x)u^2-f_2(x)u-f_3(x). \, </math>

The substitution

: <math>
\begin{align}
\xi & = \int f_3(x)E^2~dx, \\[6pt]
u & = \left(y+\dfrac{f_2(x)}{3f_3(x)}\right)E^{-1}, \\[6pt]
E & = \exp\left(\int\left(f_1(x)-\frac{f_2^2(x)}{3f_3(x)}\right)~dx\right)
\end{align}
</math>

brings the Abel equation of the first kind to the [[canonical form]]

:<math>u'=u^3+\phi(\xi). \, </math>

[[Dimitrios E. Panayotounakos]] and [[Theodoros I. Zarmpoutis]] discovered an analytic method to solve the above equation in an implicit form.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Panayotounakos | first1=Dimitrios E. | last2=Zarmpoutis | first2=Theodoros I. | title=Construction of Exact Parametric or Closed Form Solutions of Some Unsolvable Classes of Nonlinear ODEs (Abel's Nonlinear ODEs of the First Kind and Relative Degenerate Equations) | journal=International Journal of Mathematics and Mathematical Sciences | publisher=Hindawi Publishing Corporation | volume=2011 | year=2011 | pages=1–13 | doi=10.1155/2011/387429 | doi-access=free }}</ref>
